title: G4: Reduction pair processor for relative DP problems

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Adapt the reduction pair processor and prove soundness in the relative setting.

**Conjectured statement.** Let $(\succsim,\succ)$ be a reduction pair (stable monotone quasi-order $\succsim$; well-founded stable order $\succ$; $\succsim\circ\succ\subseteq\succ$). If
$$R\cup S\subseteq\succsim,\qquad \mathcal P\subseteq\succ\cup\succsim,$$
then the relative DP problem $(\mathcal P,R,S)$ is finite iff $(\mathcal P\setminus\succ,\,R,\,S)$ is.

**Why hard / must prove:**
- Crucially must **not** require $\mathrm{SN}(\to_S)$ — put both $R$ and $S$ in $\succsim$ only. (Example $R=\{a\to b\},S=\{b\to b\}$: $S$ nonterminating yet $\mathrm{SN}(R/S)$.)
- Prove that along an infinite relative chain, every step is weakly decreasing ($\succsim$) and pairs in $\succ$ strictly decrease, so a $\succ$-pair used infinitely often contradicts well-foundedness of $\succ$ — but the $\to_S^*$ connections must only weakly decrease; verify $S\subseteq\succsim$ suffices.
- State whether *strict* monotonicity is needed and on which symbols (marked vs unmarked).

Deliver full soundness proof.
